title: Sum of Shapley values
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the subsets of $\{1,ldots,n\}$. Choose a subset $S$ by first choosing its cardinality uniformly from $0,\ldots,n$, then choosing uniformly among subsets of that cardinality; for each element $i$, define its Shapley value as the expected value of $f(S\cup\{i\})-f(S\setminus\{i\})$. The sum of these values over all $i$ is $f(\{1,\ldots,n\})-f(\varnothing)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on subsets of an $n$-element set
